title: Lecture 5 — truth tables and Boolean algebra
summary: A truth table can be translated mechanically into canonical sum-of-products or product-of-sums form. Boolean identities then reduce that equation while preserving the exact same input-output behaviour.
body:
A combinational circuit is specified by its current inputs and outputs, without memory. Start from the truth table, form one minterm for every row where the output is $1$, and OR those terms to obtain canonical SOP. Alternatively, form one maxterm for every row where the output is $0$, and AND those terms to obtain canonical POS.

$$F(A,B)=\sum m(i)=\prod M(j)$$

The two canonical equations describe the same finite function. Boolean identities—especially distributivity, covering, combining, and complements—can then reduce the number of terms and literals without changing any truth-table row.
